page: Amazon Web Services r5b.4xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor running at a base clock of 3.1 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The instance allocates 16 virtual CPUs across 8 physical cores using simultaneous multithreading. Memory capacity is configured at 128.0 GB of DDR4 RAM operating at 3 GHz, providing an 8.0 GB RAM-to-core ratio. The instance includes a baseline network speed of 5 Gbps, does not contain local storage devices, and features zero dedicated GPU accelerators.

Benchmark analysis reflects typical characteristics for its hardware generation. Multithreaded tasks show balanced throughput, demonstrated by an average tier PassMark CPU score of 14,306.45, a multi-core Geekbench score of 6,974.0, and a stress-ng multi-core result of 13,988.78. Conversely, single-core execution sits in the lower tier, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1,133.0 and stress-ng single-core output of 1,327.69. Memory subsystems show stable enterprise behavior, yielding uncached read bandwidth of 87.05 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 46.8 GB/sec.

Hardware tradeoffs center around high memory density alongside lower single-threaded processing rates. While compression routines like single-threaded gzip show weaker execution rates, the server sustains 13.15 million Redis SET operations per second and handles 5,119.53 PassMark database operations. Workload efficiency is highest for in-memory databases, distributed caching layers, data processing, and enterprise application tiers requiring substantial memory footprints without demanding top-tier per-core clock speed.
